AETHERFORGE — THE BRASS PROMISE / V11 GPT IMAGES CONCEPT PAINTINGS

Make original professional production concept illustration intended to guide future stylized 3D game assets. Painted believable volume, expressive mature faces or purposeful machine anatomy, functional material thickness, deliberate large readable forms, quiet surfaces between details. The world is Brumaferrea, an original terrestrial industrial fantasy city, mournful, adult and slightly sinister. BioShock and BioShock 2 inform occupational silhouettes, failed Art Deco institutional design and repaired industrial equipment, NOT copied franchise characters or Rapture.

The user accepted the NEW WARM PALETTE. Approximate color/value targets: archive paper / warm putty #BFB49E; soot charcoal #241F1A; tobacco casing #40332B; oxidized oxblood enamel #6C3A32; aged brass #B99B63; old linen / porcelain #E4D8B7; restrained ether accent #97A581. These are art-direction guides, not a demand for exact flat hex fills. Keep material variation, but NO dominant blue or petroleum/teal background, no cyan/gold gradient, no blue luminous fog, no glowing vignette. Small jade ether accents only where justified. No shiny all-gold armor.

This request is for genuine GPT Images concept PAINTINGS. Do not emulate blocky procedural figures, low-poly maquettes, primitive Three.js models, plastic toys, chibi, photoreal cosplay or a generic polished superhero poster. Use purposeful painterly edges and material separation, without noisy texture on every surface. Any exposed person is an adult with practical work equipment, visible human character and a burdened grounded stance.

Horizontal source-art sheet, preferably 16:9 at a supported native high resolution. If the model's actual native landscape output is 1536x1024, keep that native format rather than stretching/cropping actors to imitate 16:9 or claiming an upscale is native 2K. Generous margins around heads, feet, tools, tails, rotors and weapons. Exactly the subjects described by the specific job, no extra figures. No lettering, captions, labels, numbers, brand logos, UI windows or decorative poster border. Typesetting belongs in a separate later composition, not in the generated painting.

Original split-arch workshop motif may be used very sparingly: three arch ribs interrupted by one vertical seam. It is an Aetherforge design proposal, not a BioShock logo. Avoid ornamental gear wallpaper, random tubes and copied franchise weapons, diving faces, drills, bird masks, giant syringes or recognizable Big Daddy / Big Sister / Little Sister silhouettes.

SPECIFIC JOB G01:

Create a beautiful professional hand-painted character CONCEPT ART lineup for AETHERFORGE, an original mournful industrial steampunk fantasy RPG. Three NEW original full-body adult expedition members, equally spaced, head to boots entirely visible, anatomically credible weight-bearing poses and expressive mature imperfect human faces. This is polished evocative production illustration with painterly edges, intentional design, believable material thickness and strong readable large shapes, NOT a low-poly render, NOT primitive geometry, NOT a procedural maquette, NOT toy proportions, NOT photoreal cosplay. Quiet matte warm smoke-brown and putty-gray paper studio background, soft grounded shadows, NO BLUE OR TEAL background, no cyan/gold gradient, no glowing vignette. Palette: soot charcoal, tobacco brown, oxidized iron, oxblood enamel, old linen, muted ochre and aged brass. Only a single very small jade ether accent on the healer. Study the mature occupational silhouettes, industrial repair and failed Art Deco institutional design of BioShock and BioShock 2, but make original terrestrial Brumaferrea characters, not underwater Rapture and no recognizable franchise characters. LEFT: the GUNSLINGER, an adult woman railway inspector with cropped dark hair, a tired exposed face, a narrow long tobacco-brown coat split into two large panels and an ivory diagonal inspection sash; holds a practical horizontal wood-stock pressure rifle with one thick stepped brass receiver, no random gears. CENTER: the BOILER GUARD, older broad-shouldered worker, visible worn human face below a compact angular protective helmet, grounded asymmetrical burdened stance; soot-black pressure work armor, dark oxblood enamel breastplate, flat rear pressure pack and short maintenance hammer; large RECTANGULAR SHIELD with ONE chipped ochre vertical stripe, no circular diving face, no portholes, no drill. Shield is a practical beveled rectangular slab, not a coffin or medieval heraldic kite. RIGHT: the ETHER ALCHEMIST, adult field medic with an exhausted kind face framed by a weathered old-linen hood, folded triangular canvas cape, dark warm-gray work trousers, one canvas medical satchel and ONE small jade cartridge feeding a compact brass hand applicator, not a giant syringe. Restrained original split-arch workshop motif on at most one plaque per character. Art Deco is in stepped seams, enamel tags, careful rib rhythm and purposeful work tools, not luxury gold armor or ornamental gear wallpaper. Rich material distinctions: repaired cloth, scuffed leather, dull steel, rubbed brass only at contacts. Adult somber slightly sinister survival mood, no smiling superheroes, no chibi, no generic adventurer leather suits. Hands and tools make functional contact; clear separate limbs, no merged bodies or duplicate accessories. No lettering, labels, logos, numbers, UI or ornamental borders. No Big Daddy, Big Sister, Little Sister, Subject Delta, diving helmet, drill, bathysphere, masks or copied franchise weapons. Deliver three memorable painterly original character concepts, not recolors of prior blocky models.

Create an ORIGINAL TWO-DIMENSIONAL PAINTED CHARACTER DESIGN SHEET for an adult industrial fantasy game. Exactly three full-body characters, left to right: railway Gunslinger, Boiler Guard, Ether Alchemist. The user liked the character identities and warm palette of the previous iteration but rejected its excessively realistic, generic AI-polished finish. REBUILD THE DRAWING LANGUAGE, do not simply add a paint filter to realistic people.

VISUAL LANGUAGE — this is the central requirement:
Deliberate adult caricature and economical shape design. Angular asymmetrical faces built from a handful of planar shapes, prominent noses, tired eyes indicated by a few dark strokes, simplified mouths, heavy hands and practical boots. Unequal, intentionally designed proportions: the narrow wiry inspector, the compressed broad guard with a small head and massive trapezius, the sloping triangular medic. Convincing weight without naturalistic anatomical rendering. Faces have character through strong silhouettes and drawn marks, never through pores or photographic skin shading.
Paint with broad opaque gouache-like shapes and selective dry-brush edges, with a few scratchy charcoal contour accents. Strong local color blocks; two or three clear value masses per material.
